title: Ghana's Banking Sector Collapse, 2017-2019: Open Dataset of 418 Resolved Institutions
description:
Every financial institution whose licence the Bank of Ghana revoked in the 2017-2019 banking-sector clean-up, compiled from the regulator's own published revocation notices, together with a hand-verified analysis of why the 23 savings and loans companies and finance houses failed.

418 institutions. GHS 2.30 billion in net-worth deficits. Over 360,000 depositors.

Two datasets are published. defunct_institutions.csv lists all 418 resolved institutions with their category, revocation date, receiver, resolution mechanism and statutory basis. savings_loans_verified.csv covers the 23 savings and loans companies and finance houses in detail, coding the reasons the Bank of Ghana itself stated for each failure.

Headline findings: related-party exposure appears in 17 of the 23 stated cases, and 14 of those 17 also cite misreporting or false accounting records; institutions the Bank had determined to be insolvent held deposit-taking licences for a median of 927.5 days; and five institutions account for two thirds of the total deficit.

The three source notices are archived in the repository so that any reader can check the original wording. Every figure is reproducible from the published CSVs by a Python pipeline and a SQLite analysis layer. Corrections to published findings are recorded in CHANGELOG.md rather than made silently.

This project reports what published regulatory documents state. It does not independently allege wrongdoing by any institution or any individual.
